comments:
@trond-snekvik , well,  i'm look  new transport.c in mesh dir,  https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/7ab754d9973e7b7481658bd937e186362f603f70/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/transport.c#L75-L80
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/7ab754d9973e7b7481658bd937e186362f603f70/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/transport.c#L101-L105

`Segment array `define in both TX and RX struct, It's going to be terrifying if it supports very large data(32 Segment for example) throughput, can be replaced by `sys_slist_t` ? and currently segment for RX when received completed will be copy and copy again for decryption (this is not a good way).

I'm very confused about the current way, but I can't solve it. I hope it can help you.

Okay, this is a lot of issues for one issue, I'll try to go through them one by one.

I looked through your PR, and the first issue and its fix looks good to me, well spotted!

> Segment array define in both TX and RX struct, It's going to be terrifying if it supports very large data(32 Segment for example) throughput, can be replaced by sys_slist_t ? 

This would just move the memory to the slabs though, which would have to fit a `sys_snode_t` and a segment index. I see that this might balance out if the number of segment contexts increases without proportionately increasing the number of slabs, but in my opinion, a linked list would not necessarily be an improvement memory wise. It would be nice to reduce the memory requirement for each segmented message context though, I agree it's a problem.

> currently segment for RX when received completed will be copy and copy again for decryption (this is not a good way).

I have to disagree somewhat, this is solving a different problem: The only other way to do this in a thread safe manner would be to allocate another temporary buffer of 382 bytes on stack to assemble the encrypted packet. This makes the total stack size contribution for this function > 800 bytes. I'd rather reduce the amount of unnecessary rebuilding here, I think. Currently, we're rebuilding for every attempted decrypt, but only a small percentage of the attempts would actually manipulate the buffer. I can make a PR to reduce this problem. Optimally, the buffer should only have to be reassembled in one of two cases: We received a devkey-encrypted packet that was encrypted with our own devkey while we're a provisioner (generally shouldn't happen), or we have two appkeys with the same 7 bit ID and the same net idx, and we tried the wrong one first, which happens very rarely. Would you agree?

> while in seg_rx_alloc allocate all segment, but not to check return value of k_mem_slab_alloc, so, if no buf available, the rx->seg[j] will be set to 'NULL',

We're checking that we have enough buffers before the loop, and the result can't change, as this function is only called from the rx thread, which is collaborative. I think your change is good though, it's more flexible.

review_comments: As segments are now allocated as they're received, I think we should reduce the `k_mem_slab_num_free_get` check on line 1466 to ` (k_mem_slab_num_free_get(&segs) < 1)`. Some of the flexibility introduced by doing the allocation later is lost by requiring room for all segments from the start. We need at least 1 though to avoid sending a block ack with 0 in case none of the segments can be allocated, as this has a special "reject" meaning
